scope: First-party review of 15 tools across speech APIs, meetings, inference infrastructure, coding agents, app building, code review, multi-agent development, revenue intelligence, marketing and voice AI.

accepted.name: AssemblyAI
accepted.userValue: AssemblyAI provides pre-recorded and realtime transcription, speaker identification, audio understanding, PII redaction and a managed voice-agent API through developer endpoints.

accepted.name: Avoma
accepted.userValue: Avoma combines an AI meeting assistant with scheduling, lead routing, call scoring, coaching and revenue intelligence so customer conversations can drive follow-up work.

accepted.name: Baseten
accepted.userValue: Baseten provides managed inference infrastructure, model deployment tooling, optimized model APIs and training workflows for production AI applications.

accepted.name: Blackbox AI
accepted.userValue: Blackbox AI now centers on secure model inference and routing while also offering APIs that dispatch coding agents to repositories and a terminal agent for development work.

accepted.name: Bolt.new
accepted.userValue: Bolt lets users describe an app or website, then generates and runs the project in the browser with coding-agent iteration, templates and integrations such as Figma and GitHub.

accepted.name: CodeRabbit
accepted.userValue: CodeRabbit performs context-aware code reviews, prioritizes pull requests, analyzes changes and security issues, and supports review and planning workflows in Git platforms, IDEs, CLI and team chat.

accepted.name: CrewAI
accepted.userValue: CrewAI supports agents, crews and flows with tools, memory, guardrails and human-in-the-loop controls, plus an enterprise runtime for deployment, tracing and governance.

accepted.name: Fireflies.ai
accepted.userValue: Fireflies captures meetings, creates transcripts, summaries and action items, lets users query conversations with AskFred and provides GraphQL, webhook and MCP access to meeting data.

accepted.name: Granola
accepted.userValue: Granola records system audio rather than joining calls as a bot, combines the transcript with notes written by the user, and turns the result into structured summaries, decisions and action items.

accepted.name: Gong
accepted.userValue: Gong connects customer interactions to revenue context and provides AI applications and agents for sales engagement, forecasting, enablement, follow-ups and pipeline updates.

accepted.name: Jasper
accepted.userValue: Jasper combines marketing agents and repeatable content pipelines with brand voice, knowledge and governance controls for research, optimization, translation and campaign production.

accepted.name: Krisp
accepted.userValue: Krisp offers a bot-free AI meeting assistant, transcription and noise cancellation, plus call-center voice assistance and APIs/models for voice-AI developers.

accepted.name: Lindy
accepted.userValue: Lindy connects to a company's tools and context, then runs role-based agents for practical workflows such as updating CRM records, triaging support, analyzing funnels and monitoring operations.

accepted.name: Murf
accepted.userValue: Murf combines a voiceover studio with text-to-speech APIs and conversational-agent capabilities so teams can create narration or embed speech into products.

accepted.name: Otter.ai
accepted.userValue: Otter records or joins meetings, transcribes speech with speaker recognition, generates summaries and action items, and lets users search and ask questions across their meeting history.

notes: All accepted entries were checked against first-party product pages, help centers or developer documentation.
Blackbox AI was reclassified from Coding to AI infrastructure because its current official product centers on secure inference and model routing while retaining coding-agent APIs and CLI tools.
Avoma, Jasper and Lindy availability was updated to Free trial / Paid based on explicit official free-trial language.
No popularity, traffic, revenue, ranking or customer-count claims were used as acceptance evidence.
